attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Intermittent vaginal spotting and pelvic heaviness

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns with a history of 2020 prenatal counseling for pregnancy with prior spina bifida and presents with symptomatology that has developed gradually over the past few months. Her menstrual periods started at age 13 and were previously regular, but recently she has noted irregular light bleeding outside of her cycles.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Spina bifida cystica – meningocele (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid (high-dose) 4 mg PO daily
- Prenatal multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her mother is contacted for further history and recalls being prescribed hormonal medication early in pregnancy due to a history of miscarriage.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She is not sexually active

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She denies dysuria, vaginal discharge, or abdominal pain.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her vital signs are normal, and BMI is 21 kg/m²

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender, irregular mass high on the anterior vaginal wall, but the cervix and uterus appear grossly normal. Speculum exam shows no active bleeding or obvious lesions on the cervix. The external genitalia are unremarkable.

IMAGING:
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a 4-cm solid lesion in the upper vaginal canal with no involvement of adjacent structures.

PATHOLOGY:
Biopsy of the mass reveals cells with abundant pale cytoplasm arranged in tubulocystic and papillary structures, with occasional hobnail cells.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Elena Morales, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Prenatal counseling for 8-week pregnancy with history of previous child with neural tube defect

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She recently learned she is 8 weeks pregnant and is concerned because her previous child was born with a neural tube defect. She admits that she did not take any prenatal vitamins during her last pregnancy but has started folic acid supplementation now.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid (high-dose) 4 mg PO daily
- Prenatal multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Prior offspring with spina bifida cystica (meningocele)
- Mother with cervical cancer diagnosed age 42

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time retail associate.

IMAGING:
At 18 weeks' gestation, a fetal ultrasound shows a small sac protruding from the lower spine, covered by skin and containing meninges but no neural tissue. There is no associated hydrocephalus or cerebellar herniation.
